question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence.

She had to __break the bank__ to buy that purse.

options.text: to go as per one's budget

solution:
The correct answer is** option (1)** i.e. **"To be very expensive".** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

 
• The idiom** "break the bank"** means to use up all of one's money or resources. So in the given sentence, it implies that "she had to use a lot of money or perhaps all her savings to buy that purse".
 
• **Break the Bank** - To be very expensive; to surpass the limits of one's budget or resources. **(बहुत महँगा होना; किसी के बजट की सीमा को पार करना)**
 
 
• **Example:** Buying that luxury car would certainly** break the bank**; it's way too expensive for me.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **"To be very expensive".**
